correctness.rationale: The 3-row parity lemma is a complete combinatorial argument; backtracking over unused columns/symbols and independent symbol-permutation enumeration exhaust all order-nine transversals. Two distinct adjacency methods produce 2025 vertices, 4131 edges, four components exactly matching the four parity classes, the specified degrees and all-source diameters 8,8,8,7. Both verifier programs were actually executed with captured outputs; finite enumeration is not used to infer a higher-order theorem. A byte-exact replay path accompanies the finding.

value.rationale: Changing exactly three entries is the minimal possible nontrivial local operation between transversals, so component connectivity is the natural irreducibility question for constrained sampling/navigating transversals. The cyclic order-nine square is the first composite odd cyclic-group table with transversals. Parity completely governs its reachability even though 21 transversals are frozen already at order seven; the full 4-component census, diameters and degree strata give a useful sharp finite benchmark beyond total enumeration.
